question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Chicago, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Kavi Gupta
galleries.address_hint: 835 W Washington Blvd and 219 N Elizabeth St

notes.anthropic: Chicago's most internationally visible dealer, representing Roger Brown estate, Jeffrey Gibson, Mickalene Thomas and Deborah Kass, with heavy global fair presence.
notes.openai: Globally active gallery known for ambitious exhibitions, major art-fair participation and an influential multicultural programme.

notes.anthropic: Global platform for artists of the African diaspora (Amoako Boafo, Clotilde Jiménez); Chicago flagship with Paris and Mexico City spaces and major fair presence.
notes.openai: Internationally prominent gallery championing artists of Africa and its diaspora, with spaces in Chicago, Paris and Mexico City.

notes.anthropic: Scholarly recovery of Chicago Imagists and postwar abstraction alongside a sharp contemporary roster; a critical engine of the city's art history.
notes.openai: Internationally respected for rigorous contemporary art, Chicago modernism, artist estates, experimental music and scholarship.

notes.anthropic: Non-collecting kunsthalle founded 1915 that gave many artists their first US institutional show; still the city's most influential experimental exhibition program.
notes.openai: Historic non-collecting contemporary institution whose commissioned exhibitions and publications exert exceptional critical influence.

notes.anthropic: Launched careers of Amy Sherald, Rashid Johnson and Ebony G. Patterson; consistently ahead of institutional taste since 2000.

notes.anthropic: Ambitious roster (Harold Mendez, Alex Chitty, Bethany Collins) and strong fair record; a leading voice among Chicago's second-generation dealers.

notes.anthropic: Rigorous photo- and lens-based program that has grown into one of the city's most critically respected younger galleries, with Lisbon expansion.
notes.openai: Conceptually focused gallery and publisher whose artists receive growing international institutional and critical attention.

notes.anthropic: Since 1916 a private club with a public, non-collecting gallery of consistently first-rate international contemporary exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1939; the incubator that introduced the Hairy Who, and still the South Side's key exhibition, residency and teaching hub.
notes.openai: A foundational Chicago art center supporting experimentation, exhibitions, residencies and artist development across generations.

notes.anthropic: Drawing-centric, Imagist-adjacent program since 2004 championing artists like Dutes Miller, Deb Sokolow and Sarah and Joseph Belknap.
notes.openai: Long-running gallery recognized for idiosyncratic, materially inventive artists and a particularly strong commitment to works on paper.

notes.anthropic: Nationally significant platform for American collectible design and art-design crossovers; regular at Design Miami and EXPO Chicago.
notes.openai: Internationally influential platform at the intersection of contemporary art, collectible design, architecture and material experimentation.

notes.anthropic: Long-running West Town gallery with a crisp painting-and-object program and steady support of mid-career Chicago artists.
